title: P1.1: testbench model computes SRA as a logical shift
body:
The ALU testbench's expected value for SRA mixed signed and unsigned operands inside one `?:`, so Verilog evaluated the whole expression as unsigned and the model did a logical shift. The DUT was right; the model was wrong.

Fix: compute each case in its own statement with explicit `$signed`.

title: P1.3: testbench variable named `matches` does not compile as SystemVerilog
body:
`matches` is a reserved keyword in SystemVerilog (pattern matching). Compiling the FSM testbench with `-g2012` failed.

Fix: renamed the variable.

title: P1.4: testbench never applies reset
body:
`reg rst_n = 0;` starts at 0, so there is no negedge and an `always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)` block never sees reset. The FIFO started with X pointers.

Fix: drive reset explicitly after the clocks start (0 -> 1 with clock edges in between).

title: P1.4: $realtime counts in seconds in the async FIFO bench
body:
The RTL files had no `` `timescale ``, so the default unit made `$realtime` and the metastability window wrong.

Fix: `` `timescale 1ns/1ps `` in every RTL file.

title: P1.4: binary-pointer CDC bug passes the data checks
body:
With binary pointers synchronized (seeded `BUG_BIN`), data still arrived in order: a wrong synchronized value lasts one cycle and the equality compares hide it.

Fix (testbench): added the invariant 'the read side never sees more data than was written'. It fires 172 / 663 times at the unequal clock ratios.

title: P1.5: FIFO accepts a push while full if a pop happens the same cycle
body:
The FIFO's rule 'full + pop accepts a push' made the producer's count of accepted bytes wrong, and the UART loopback test lost track of bytes.

Fix: simpler contract `accepted = push && !full` (no combinational path from pop to push acceptance). Same change in the P1.4 FIFO.

title: P1.5: RX restarts on a framing error
body:
After a bad stop bit the line is still low, and the receiver took it as the start bit of a new frame, producing garbage bytes.

Fix: new WAIT_HI state: after a framing error, wait for the line to go high before looking for a start bit.

title: P3.3: early BVALID only caught by a timeout
body:
The seeded `BUG_EARLY_B` (B response before both AW and W were taken) made the bench hang until the timeout instead of failing with a clear message.

Fix: B-ordering monitor that checks every B against the writes accepted so far. It catches the bug with a clear message on 3 of 5 seeds; the other 2 still end in the timeout, so this stays partly open.

title: P4: register-file write-through makes a combinational loop in the single-cycle core
body:
The register file bypass (write data visible on the read port in the same cycle) is needed for WB -> ID in the pipeline, but in the single-cycle core it closes a loop: read -> ALU -> write data -> read. Simulation hung.

Fix: `BYPASS` parameter, 1 in the pipeline, 0 in the single-cycle core.

title: P4: ISA test overwrites its own case number
body:
The generated ISA test kept the failing case number in x3 (gp) and also used x3 as a result register, so a failure reported the wrong case.

Fix: case number in x28, which no test uses.

title: P4: pipeline ends the test before the TOHOST store retires
body:
The testbench detected the store to TOHOST on the data-memory port (MEM stage), two cycles before it retired, so the last instructions were missing from the trace.

Fix: detect TOHOST from the retirement port.

title: P4: DPI-C reference model does not link
body:
Verilator compiles the C file as C++, so the exported functions got mangled names and the link failed.

Fix: wrap the DPI functions in `extern "C"`.

title: P4: random programs store registers that were never written
body:
The core's register file has no reset (X), the C model starts at 0. A random program that stored an unwritten register (for example the loop counter x30) gave a mismatch that was not a core bug.

Fix: the generator writes x1-x30 with random values first.

title: P5.1: formal properties see free signals instead of the FIFO pointers
body:
The properties were in a wrapper and used hierarchical names (`dut.wptr`). Yosys does not resolve those before flattening, so they became unconstrained wires and the base case failed on impossible traces.

Fix: include the properties inside the FIFO under `` `ifdef FORMAL ``.

title: P5.2: gate-level simulation does not elaborate
body:
The Yosys netlist has no parameters (they are fixed at synthesis), but the RTL testbench passes DIVISOR/PAR_EN/PAR_ODD, so elaboration failed.

Fix: a thin shim module with the original parameters that checks them and instantiates the netlist.

title: P5.5: false failures from the testbench ($countones, array overflow)
body:
Two testbench bugs: `$countones` returned wrong values in Icarus 12 inside this expression, and the skid/FIFO scoreboard arrays overflowed after 4,096 / 8,192 words.

Fix: a small `ones4` function, and indexes that wrap.

title: P5.7: first beat of a back-to-back matrix is lost
body:
The testbench drove the next matrix while the array was still reading out the previous one (in_ready low), so the first beat was dropped and every result was missing one product.

Fix: the testbench now waits for in_ready (proper valid/ready), and the design accepts a new beat on the last read-out row and clears the accumulators there, so matrices follow with no gap.
